text: string “extr” default argument extr_def within extractant_average() can adapted reflect mapping. Like std_blank_average(), extractant_average() computes per-plate average, standard deviation coefficient variation (%) blanks. Tip 1: 1 extractant per plate? extractant_average() also works several extractants per plate, argument extr_def must given vector defining extractants (e.g., extr_def = c("extr_1", "extr_2"). Note complicates bit process line need attribute extractant sample based something just plate identifier. See also ?extractant_average() examples [multiple-extractants section](#sec-multiple-extr)

title: Extraction and Quality Check (QC) of blank values for standard curves — extract_std_blank
text: extract_std_blank() works steps: - First, data corresponding wells containing standard curve extracted (defined parameter std_def) - Second, within "standard data", dataset, plate column (= 1 curve), smallest absorbance value extracted. - check smallest per-curve value indeed found plate row "" (top_down pipetting) row "H" (bottom_up pipetting). - case, wells considered "untrusted" removed "trusted" blank values. Per-plate averages computed separately, std_blank_average() — deliberately kept step, taken whichever $/ $trusted/$untrusted (possibly manually reviewed/edited) user decides trust.

text: Wraps plot_std(), called model = "linear" model = "poly", combined side side. plot_std() fits model internally purely drawing — function use fit_curve_models()'s output, since separate (equivalent) fit done different purpose (inspecting actual model object, e.g. plot_residual_comparison()).

title: Plot linear and polynomial model fits side by side for one or more curves — plot_model_comparison
code: plot_model_comparison(   curve_data,   conc_col = "std_conc",   value_col = "abs_corrected",   curve_id_col = "unique_curve_id",   colour_col = NULL,   through_origin = TRUE,   unit_col = NULL,   smooth_alpha = 0.3,   smooth_linewidth = 0.5,   smooth_linetype = 2,   legend_position = "right" )

title: Plot linear and polynomial model fits side by side for one or more curves — plot_model_comparison
text: curve_data tibble data one curve, several curves (grouped/coloured curve_id_col) want overplotted comparison across multiple curves. conc_col Name column containing concentration. Defaults "std_conc". value_col Name column containing (blank-corrected) absorbance. Defaults "abs_corrected". curve_id_col Name column identifying curve row belongs , used grouping/colouring. Defaults "unique_curve_id". colour_col Name column used colour/fill. NULL (default), uses curve_id_col. Set independently colour something meaningful comparing several curves (e.g. date, dilution factor). through_origin Whether force fits origin. Defaults TRUE. See fit_curve_models() argument's meaning. unit_col Passed plot_std() — optionally shows concentration unit x-axis. NULL (default) shows unit. See plot_std()'s unit_col argument full behavior (literal string column name). smooth_alpha, smooth_linewidth, smooth_linetype Passed plot_std() — control fitted smooth-curve's visibility. Defaults match plot_std()'s defaults. legend_position Standard ggplot2 legend.position value colour legend. Defaults "none". meaningful colour_col (default curve-id grouping) produces legend worth showing — e.g. comparing multiple curves via review_model_choice()'s overplot = TRUE mode.

title: Plot linear and polynomial model fits side by side for one or more curves — plot_model_comparison
text: combined patchwork figure (linear model plot next polynomial model plot).

title: Boxplot + ridgeline pair for one chunk of samples — plot_qc_sample_pair
text: Builds one combined QC figure chunk samples: labelled boxplot (boxplot_values()) next ridgeline density plot (plot_ridges_values()), sharing one centered axis sample identities . ridge makes easy spot outlier glance; paired boxplot gives exact well_id remove via remove_wells(). whole pair enclosed border box. Typically built per chunk samples plot_list_qc_samples() rather called directly.

title: Boxplot + ridgeline pair for one chunk of samples — plot_qc_sample_pair
text: chunk vector values y_col include pair (one "page" worth samples). data tibble containing columns referenced y_col, value_col, (given) colour_col. y_col Name column identifying samples — shared boxplot ridge plot row/category axis. value_col Name numeric column visualize. value_range length-2 numeric vector giving shared value-axis range use, samples can compared fairly regardless chunk land . Typically computed (across whole dataset) plot_list_qc_samples() passed . colour_col Optional colour: NULL default colour, literal colour name, name column data — passed boxplot_values() plot_ridges_values(). scale Passed plot_ridges_values() — far ridge extends beyond row. Defaults 0.8, keeps ridges close enough row stay visually aligned paired boxplot. title Optional title pair, shown centered shared axis. Defaults y_col's name given. border_colour Colour border box drawn around pair. Defaults "grey80". legend_position Standard ggplot2 legend.position value (e.g. "none", "right", "bottom", "left", "top"), applied boxplot ridge, duplicate legends automatically collected one shared legend pair. Defaults "none" (legend shown).

what: Plot residuals of linear vs. polynomial models for one curve — plot_residual_comparison
title: Plot residuals of linear vs. polynomial models for one curve — plot_residual_comparison
text: Compares model's residuals scatter around zero across range concentrations, one standard curve. Residuals close zero systematic pattern indicate good fit; curved systematic pattern (typically linear model's residuals, polynomial fit actually needed) sign model capture true shape curve.

title: Plot residuals of linear vs. polynomial models for one curve — plot_residual_comparison
code: plot_residual_comparison(curve_data, models, conc_col = "std_conc")

title: Plot residuals of linear vs. polynomial models for one curve — plot_residual_comparison
text: curve_data tibble data curve, column referenced conc_col. Must data used fit models (row order/count) — e.g. via fit_curve_models(). Note: curve_data contains rows NA fitted value/concentration columns, lm() silently drops , can misalign residuals curve_data's concentration values . currently guarded — worth keeping curve data free NAs relevant columns. models named list linear poly elements, lm model object — typically output fit_curve_models(). conc_col Name column containing concentration. Defaults "std_conc".

title: Display one or more standard curve(s) — plot_std
text: std_data table containing data plotted. Must contain columns referenced conc_col, value_col, group_col, label_col, unit_col. plot shows many curves, consider filtering input data frame adding ggplot layer facet (see ?facet_wrap() ?facet_grid()). through_origin Whether smooth curve constrained go origin. Default TRUE, makes sense absorbance data already blank-corrected model model use smooth curve. Accepts either linear (default) poly polynomial model (y = ax + bx^2 + c, c = 0 through_origin = TRUE) conc_col Name column containing concentration. Defaults "std_conc". value_col Name column containing absorbance. Defaults "abs". group_col Name column used group/colour/fill curves (e.g. one curve per plate). Defaults "column". colour_col Name column used colour/fill. NULL (default), uses group_col (variable drives grouping colour, originally). Set independently colour something else meaningful (e.g. date, dilution factor) still fitting one regression line per group_col. label_col Name column used label individual points. Defaults "well_id". unit_col Optional: label concentration unit x-axis. NULL (default) shows unit . Otherwise, either name column std_data read unit , literal string (e.g. "mg/L") applied uniformly. smooth_alpha Transparency fitted smooth-curve ribbon/line. Defaults 0.3. smooth_linewidth Width fitted smooth-curve line. Defaults 0.5. smooth_linetype Line type fitted smooth-curve line (ggplot2 linetype code). Defaults 2 (dashed).

what: Quality Check (QC) of raw absorbance data — qc_raw_abs
title: Quality Check (QC) of raw absorbance data — qc_raw_abs
text: qc_raw_abs() extracts data relating wells absorbance outside user-defined range. Whereas long-lasting tradition setting "acceptable" absorbance values 0.1 1 (default values function), reality, acceptable range depend experiment, usage quality spectrophotomer. Note values lower 0.1 rare, especially blank lower values standard curve.

title: Quality Check (QC) of raw absorbance data — qc_raw_abs
code: qc_raw_abs(   data,   value_col = "abs",   map_col = "map",   dataset_col = "dataset",   plate_id_col = "plate_id",   well_id_col = "well_id",   min_abs = 0.1,   max_abs = 1,   empty_wells = "empty",   show_msg = TRUE,   show_warning = TRUE,   show_plot = TRUE,   plot_binwidth = 0.01,   plot_col_facet = "dataset",   export_plot = NULL )

title: Quality Check (QC) of raw absorbance data — qc_raw_abs
text: data Tibble, similar form tidy_table. particular, columns referenced map_col, value_col, dataset_col, plate_id_col, well_id_col must present. value_col Name column containing absorbance (another numeric value like QC). Defaults "abs". map_col Name column containing well mapping/type information, used identify empty wells. Defaults "map". dataset_col, plate_id_col, well_id_col Names columns identifying dataset, plate, well — used report wells suspicious. Default "dataset", "plate_id", "well_id" respectively. min_abs, max_abs Lowest highest accepted value absorbance, default 0.1 1, respectively. empty_wells Character string corresponding empty wells described plate mapping. Defaults "empty", can also vector containing several values. Note wells described NA map column also ignored. show_msg, show_warning Whether keep (TRUE) suppress (FALSE) message warning returned case absence (message) presence (warning) suspicious, --range, wells show_plot Whether display associated plot (histogram absorbance values). Default TRUE. Note next arguments relevant show_plot = TRUE. plot_binwidth set binwidth histogram. Default 0.01 plot_col_facet column use facet plots. facetting, use NULL (legacy "none" string still accepted , backward compatibility). Defaults "dataset". (now, facet 1 axis possible) export_plot Defaults null. Set string save plot global environment, string name object (e.g., export_plot = "abs_distrib" save object called abs_distrib)

title: Quality Check (QC) of raw absorbance data — qc_raw_abs
text: table 5 columns. first 3 (dataset, plate_id, well_id) allow unique identification suspicious wells can used run remove_wells(). next 2 columns (map, abs) allow visualization suspicious wells

text: Samples (uses ) curves data, fits linear polynomial model , builds comparison + residual plots help decide model appropriate. Defaults "unique_curve_id". conc_col Name column containing concentration. Defaults "std_conc". value_col Name column containing (blank-corrected) absorbance. Defaults "abs_corrected". through_origin Whether force models origin. Defaults TRUE. unit_col Passed plot_model_comparison() / plot_std(). title: Compute per-dilution Averages for Standard Curves — std_dilution_average
text: Averages absorbance per plate, per row (dilution level), across several standard curves pipetted plate — useful plate holds one curve standard solution (e.g. one column 1, one column 12). Averaging serves two purposes: reducing noise model fitting, correcting systematic drift curves caused pipetting order (plate typically pipetted left right, column 1 column 12 wells experience slightly different incubation times reading — averaging across plate's curves compensates , since -row wells across curves assumed hold concentration).

title: Tidying plate data (verticalization) — verticalize_plates
text: tibble tibble containing raw plate-formatted data tidied. tibble must fit following criteria: - Plate ids single capital letter (e.g., "", "B", ...) - Plates must complete (96 wells accounted , set 12 columns x 8 rows), may contain NA's - Plate data tibble must structured exactly example files (see also txt_to_tibble(), csv_to_tibble() skanit_to_tibble()). coerce_numeric Whether force data entries numerical. default set FALSE, data outputted strings prefix Defaults empty string. prefix can added column names, can useful join tables distinct datasets row_col Name column identifying plate row (-H) raw input. Defaults "row". column_cols vector 12 column names holding plate columns 1-12 raw input, order. Defaults paste0("X", 1:12).
